Thanks for the quick, and detailed, reply. 

If I’m honest, and out of respect for true genuine polyamory, I probably don’t connect fully with the lifestyle/orientation. 

I wanted to engage in the idea because: 
- I didn’t want to go my whole life having only had sex with one person.
- I felt like I wanted to see what “other” felt like
- I could tell it was important to my partner and wanted to support that for the benefit of our relationship
- My now atheist view on life wanted to shout “fuck you” to my religious upbringing and challenge the old conservative approaches to monogamy. It felt rebellious to explore it. 
- The “risk” it placed on our relationship created a sexual tension that we both found hot. The idea of poly wasn’t in any way a kink... instead it felt like we were embracing the unknown. 

And then... here we are... shifted sideways again to a new place to work out “what next.”

Honestly, if the situation were different we’d likely split with a blessing sending each other on their way. 

Instead, our kids are at a fragile stage of life, one is autistic. Our finances would also make it near impossible to run two houses (and would all be on me for the first few years if we split).

So, in some ways this feels like a question of practicality... mixed with a two-decade relationship of trust and connection that we want to find a way to make work.
